title: Opposed Asymmetric Blades And Oval Shaft Kayak Paddle
description: One newly authored whole fixed double-ended kayak-paddle-inspired decorative display lying flat. A long complete oval-section shaft joins two opposed asymmetric tapered blades with finite bevelled edges and broad subtly ridged faces. Two whole bored drip-collar forms embrace the shaft near the blade roots, and one complete central sleeve marks the fixed centre joint. Six closed whole components, three opaque constant PBR roles, metres Z up and horizontal bounds-centred ground datum. Both blade backs have finite flat dry-display patches; there is no boat, water or occupant. All longitudinal blade stations, asymmetry and joining geometry are newly authored, not two extracted work-skiff or rowing-scull blades, a duplicated tennis paddle, or a sliced old boat. One original model and zero scenes. Static simplified exterior only: the two blades are fixed in one unfeathered pose, with no shaft assembly, angle adjustment, paddle fit, water interaction, propulsion, hydrodynamics, strength, loading, balance, manufacture or water-safety capability. No rigging, animation or interaction.
